text: Fresh shall count a pass only while the artifacts it verified are unchanged since the check ran.
rationale: vv counts a pass forever. On vv's own folder, breaking lint() left the report at 19/19 verified until someone reran the tests (mozzie-stale.mjs, part 1).

text: Fresh shall bind each piece of evidence to the content of what it verified.
rationale: vv's evidence carries a date and nothing else, so it cannot tell whether it is still about the code in front of it.

text: Each evidence entry Fresh writes shall carry the SHA-256 of every artifact that implements the requirements its check verifies, taken before the check starts.
acceptance: T-EV-DIGEST passes: for a fixture of 3 artifacts and 4 checks, every written entry lists exactly the traced artifacts with digests equal to sha256 of the file bytes at start.
rationale: Digest at start, not finish: an edit during the run must make the result stale, not certify the edit.

text: Fresh shall drop evidence whose recorded digest differs from an artifact's current digest, then call vv's status unchanged on what remains.
acceptance: T-EV-FILTER passes: one byte changed in one artifact turns exactly the requirements it implements from verified to unverified, and no others.
rationale: A stale pass becomes unknown, not failed. Fresh says what it cannot vouch for; it does not guess.

text: With no artifact changed, Fresh's report shall equal vv's report on the same folder.
acceptance: T-EV-VVSAME passes on vv's own folder and on both other proposals' requirement sets with synthetic evidence.
rationale: Fresh is a filter in front of vv, not a second vv. vv stays read-only and stays the only place status is computed.

text: Fresh shall list every leaf with a verifies link and no implements link, and shall count its evidence as vv does.
acceptance: T-EV-NOIMPL passes: the list is sorted, complete on a fixture with 2 such leaves, and their status matches vv's.
rationale: A requirement traced to no artifact cannot go stale, which also means nobody can tell when it should. Naming them is the honest part.

text: The des controller shall rerun the checks traced to an edited artifact, one runner at a time, and write their evidence.
rationale: Filtering alone turns stale into unknown; something has to turn unknown back into known.

text: On an edit signal, the controller shall queue exactly the checks that verify requirements implemented by the edited artifact.
acceptance: T-CTL-TRACED passes on a fixture with known links: the queued set equals the set computed by hand from links.json.
rationale: In the sizing, traced reruns left about a third of the wrongly-verified hours of 'rerun all' (0.48 against 1.53), at about a third of the runner time.

text: A check already queued shall not be queued twice, and a check whose artifact is edited while it runs shall be queued again.
acceptance: T-CTL-COALESCE passes: 5 edits in a burst produce one run per check, plus one rerun for the check that was mid-run.
rationale: Without the first rule the queue grows with typing speed; without the second, a run finishes against code that has already changed.

text: The same edit sequence shall produce the same queue order and evidence under run() and under runRealtime() with a fake clock.
acceptance: T-CTL-SAME passes: logs compared entry by entry.
rationale: The sizing is only about the controller if it is the same controller.

text: The controller shall append every edit signal, queue decision and check result to a log that replays through run() to the same evidence.
rationale: When someone asks why a requirement went unverified at 14:02, the log answers.

text: The sizing shall state what each policy costs in wrongly-verified requirement-hours, honestly-unknown requirement-hours and runner time.
rationale: The choice between policies is a trade, and the trade should be in numbers before anyone picks.

text: Traced reruns shall leave at most 1.0 wrongly-verified requirement-hour per day under the stated assumptions.
acceptance: A-PWR-TRACED over 1000 seeded days writes TPM-FALSE-VERIFIED; sized at 0.48 (seed block 1) and 0.50 (block 7).
rationale: Against 12.2 for vv today with a day-end run. Threshold doubled from the sized figure because the edit and break rates are invented.

text: Traced reruns shall use at most half the runner time of rerunning the whole suite on every edit.
rationale: If traced reruns cost as much as running everything, the trace is clutter and 'rerun all' is simpler.

text: The report shall print the requirement-hours shown as unknown under the freshness filter beside the assumptions that produced them.
acceptance: The A-PWR output lists edit rate, break rate, fix rate, suite size and check durations next to the figure (sized at 20.6 req-h/day).
rationale: The filter's zero wrongly-verified hours is true by construction. Its cost is the unknown hours, and that is the number to argue about.

text: Fresh shall be shown to hold on a project with a history that nobody here wrote.
rationale: Every rate in the sizing is assumed.

text: The edit, break and fix rates shall be replaced by rates measured from a real repository's commit and test history.
acceptance: Rates measured from at least 3 months of one project's history, with the sizing rerun on them and the TPMs re-recorded.
rationale: Our own folders reset every session and have no history worth the name.

text: A project shall run Fresh for one month and its log shall show at least one pass that vv alone would still have counted after the code changed.
acceptance: The log entry, the edit that staled it, and the rerun result, named by the project, not by us.
rationale: If a month passes with no such catch, Fresh is solving a problem that project doesn't have, and should be dropped there.
